subject: SLO & regional routing follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Marsh <alex@peregrine.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: SLO & regional routing follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can align the technical follow-up: 

Summary notes
- Primary workload: conversational search + short-context summarization (~128 tokens typical).
- Expected sustained throughput: ~120 req/s across global peak, with regional peaks varying (US 60rps, EU 35rps, APAC 25rps).
- Concurrency: expected 350 concurrent request slots at peak; prefer per-region concurrency caps.
- Streaming: client expects partial/chunked responses for longer generations; first-byte latency is important (per-region first-byte SLO).
- Data residency: EU customer data must stay within EU data plane; APAC has a preference for regional processing but can failover to US if capacity-constrained with explicit logging/consent.

Asks / action items for Peregrine (please confirm):
1) Confirm peak rps numbers per region (US/EU/APAC) and percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests.
2) Clarify worst-case token lengths for streaming sessions (so we can size KV-cache and batching).
3) Any regulatory constraints beyond EU residency (e.g., specific countries in APAC requiring on-prem).

What we will provide next
- SLO matrix (attached) with recommended 50/95/99 p95 targets for first-byte and tail latency by region.
- Regional routing playbook: how we route by region, failover tiers, and expected unit economics.
- Short security note on how EU residency is enforced via private VPC peering and data-plane segmentation.

Proposed next step: 30-min technical sync with engineering (Marissa + Aditya in copy) — are you available Fri 20th 9:00–9:30am PST or Mon 23rd?

Thanks,
Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Marsh <alex@peregrine.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@peregrine.health>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:33:00 +0100
Subject: Re: SLO & regional routing follow-up

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with infra: 

- APAC peak is likely higher than estimated if our user base in India spikes during launches; can we treat APAC as a 40rps regional peak buffer for sizing?
- Streaming ratio: about 18% of calls are streaming; most streams are short (avg 2–3 chunks) but we do have occasional long sessions (~800 tokens).
- First-byte expectation: our product team wants <150ms first-byte for interactive streams in US/EU; APAC can tolerate higher but prefer <250ms. Is that feasible with Redwood's routing?

Also: If we have to failover APAC traffic to US, we need explicit visibility and audit logs for residency-sensitive sessions. Finally, is there a recommended model-variant for cost/latency tradeoff when routing off-region?

On the Fri slot: Fri 20th 9:00am PST works for Priya and me.

Best,
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Marsh <alex@peregrine.health>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@peregrine.health>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO & regional routing follow-up

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the quick turn. A few concrete items from our SRE/product side based on your numbers and the call: 

1) APAC sizing: treat APAC peak as 40rps for capacity planning. We'll reserve a buffer tier for bursts + one fast-failover lane to US if capacity is exhausted.

2) Streaming SLOs (proposed, per-region p95):
   - US: first-byte < 120ms, tail (complete response) < 400ms for typical short streams (<=300 tokens).
   - EU: first-byte < 140ms, tail < 450ms.
   - APAC: first-byte < 220ms, tail < 600ms.
These are initial recommendations; we'll tune after the technical sync and based on measured RTTs from your frontends.

3) Concurrency and batching: we'll configure per-region concurrency caps (US 180, EU 100, APAC 70) and adaptive batching to balance throughput/cost. With 800-token worst-case streams we will increase KV-cache allocation and recommend a longer prefetch window for caching.

4) Regional routing policy: default is "region-preferred" (serve locally if capacity available), then "region-tier-fallback" (fallback to nearest available region by latency tier). When routing across residency boundaries (e.g., EU->US), we will mark sessions as "residency-exempt" only with your explicit consent and provide logging at request-id level.

5) Model fallback: suggest using the same model family but a smaller quantized variant (e.g., small-llm-q4) for off-region failover to preserve semantics while reducing cost/latency risk. We'll include regression metrics in the playbook.

Attachments: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO table by region), network-topology-diagram.pdf (high-level peering notes).

Next steps:
- Confirm APAC 40rps assumption and streaming % (Alex/Priya).
- Technical sync Fri 20th 9:00am PST — sending calendar invite now.
- Prep list for the sync: sample request traces, a small set of prompt/test cases for streaming verification, and any country-specific residency constraints.

Jordan, Aditya: can you add a short note on audit/logging retention policy we will offer (30/90/365 days options) so Alex can surface to compliance?

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0199

Thanks Marissa — that all looks reasonable. Confirming APAC 40rps and streaming ~18%. We can provide a small set of sample traces + a doc listing country-specific residency restrictions before the sync.

Please send the calendar invite for 9:00am PST and include the technical deck. Also, we'll need SOC 2 evidence and a short note on retention options (30/90/365) before we go to procurement.

See you on the call.

Alex
